notes: Native oracle: OpenTofu 1.13.0 show -json -config and graph -type=plan on every .tf directory (19 roots per subject), after init -backend=false -get=false. All roots succeeded, all 3,111 definitions were located, and the two raw truth JSON files were byte-identical before and after the engine fix. The exact Git tracked sets, measured file lists and pinned module manifests also match. Providers came only from a private filesystem mirror, modules from exact pinned Git checkouts; no plan, apply or cloud API was run. AWS 6.67.0 was identified in the previous reading; seven ancillary provider versions and ten registry module versions are newly pinned compatible inputs, not proven copies of the old mirror. Counts and digests: docs/assessments/data/terraform-two-hop-2026-10-26/summary.json.

The reading uses the median CPU-throughput run. L1 and L2 grades are excellent and excellent, respectively.

L3 limits: the repaired engine emits 13 cross-file pairs beyond the native set. The earlier reading attributed beyond-tool references to local values and dynamic blocks missing from OpenTofu's reduced plan graph or configuration JSON; this rerun did not individually re-adjudicate those 13. The native oracle scores file-granularity destinations, not typed attribute binding. The recovered 1381 pairs show the repair's measured effect; this aggregate result does not itself classify every historical miss by cause. Registry, remote, escaping, caller-directory and nonliteral module sources remain outside the repaired two-hop strategy.

Independence: a provider-free fixture's native raw truth changes when a source fact changes. A separate document-fixture replay changes real Terraform extractor output while the raw native truth remains identical before and after; other exercised document extraction and mixed-dialect fixture results stay stable. The replay is fixture coverage, not full-subject regrading of other document dialects. See docs/assessments/2026-10-26-iac-docxref-impact.md.
Per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile; an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing.
